correctness.rationale: For n>=2, 1<=s=k+1<=n, lambda>=0, minimum l1 distance to sparse l1 unit sphere is t-T_s+|T_s-1|. Support-wise triangle inequality is attained by matching signs and adjusting nonnegative masses. Distance to its lambda-ball thickening is max(0,dist-lambda). Largest-s coordinate averaging T_s>=s t/n is sharp exactly for equal moduli (when t>0); the residual convex piecewise-affine function is maximized at t=0 or 1+lambda. This yields max{0,1-lambda,2[1-s(1+lambda)/n]}, saturation threshold, and origin/boundary/equal-modulus extremizers including critical 2s=n. No finite grid is used as proof.
residual_risks: For the displayed equality case at lambda equal threshold the Hausdorff defect is zero and every hull point is a maximizer; the extremizer classification is explicitly only in positive-defect regime.
